srcs: Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission, Cause 46276 order (Indiana Michigan Power / Google, Fort Wayne): "The Contract also contains demand response obligations designed to reduce I&M's peak load and capacity obligations"; specified interruptible load and curtailment parameters (checked by Claude) source OPERATOR CLAIM: Enel X case study, Digital Realty Ireland: nine data centres in EirGrid DS3 frequency response; "when the grid frequency drops below 50Hz, the data centre can safely draw some power from its batteries" source VENDOR CLAIM: Fluence 2022, Google St. Ghislain, Belgium: 2.75 MW / 5.5 MWh battery replacing diesel backup and in Elia's ancillary-services market; a "proof-of-concept" source BC Hydro 2026 Call for Demand RFA: 100 + 300 MW; 10–145 MW per project; ≥10% premium; curtailment; heat-recovery-ready inside the 10% environmental weight source AESO, Operating reserve (ancillary services) source regulation Data Centre Regulation, Alta Reg 117/2026 under the Electric Utilities Act (King's Printer extract, current as of 9 Jun 2026; J.B. PDF 16 Oct 2026). s. 1: data centre includes hosting/cloud, digital asset mining, AI/ML, content delivery. s. 2: "large data centre" = maximum demand directly from the transmission system of 75 MW or more, or a lower threshold the AESO sets for reliability. s. 3: AESO may aggregate integrated data centres on the same or adjacent parcels with the same owner or affiliate. s. 5: a large data centre may be "tethered" to new or added generating units or energy storage able to supply at least its maximum demand, reliably and predictably (the Regulation does not limit the fuel; AESO's first intake does). s. 6: tethered requests processed first. s. 7: AESO may require site control, municipal zoning approvals, financing, permits or water licences. s. 8: no service above the tethered supply. s. 9: bridged service before the supply runs only once the plant is approved by the AUC, max 3 years, AESO may cap each and all bridged loads and suspend for unmet criteria. s. 10: inadequate supply — bridged data centres reduced before all other market participants; mandatory load shed — large data centres reduced before all others. s. 12: review by 31 May 2030, expires 31 May 2035 source system operator AESO, Large Load Integration Phase 2A — Proposed BYOG Process (26 Jun 2026, proposal, not final). Applies to transmission-connected loads asking for 75 MW or more of demand transmission service (DTS), site-aggregated; excludes loads under 75 MW, distribution-connected load and storage. First intake gas-fired generation only, "net new"; tethering ratio: generator output at 25 °C, 40% humidity equals DTS contract capacity. Data centres must show municipal zoning or area-structure-plan approval and accept the data-centre connection requirements. DTS commitment fee $15k/MW (refundable). Bridging before the generator runs: at most 20/30/40% of the DTS request by generator milestone, 1,600 MW across all intakes, up to 3 years; bridging load is fully interruptible, reduced before all other non-firm load to avoid a shortfall, curtailment scheme TBD (pro rata, rotation or combination); suspended for failing to curtail source system operator AESO, Large Load Integration Phase 2A BYOG Process Update, stakeholder session deck (18 Jun 2026, updated 24 Jun 2026). About 20 GW of data-centre load requested each quarter since Q2 2025 (19.2 GW Q2 2026). Phase 2 is modular: 2A BYOG, 2B ISO tariff, 2C "Grid Partners" (flexible load structures, operating procedures, market products), not yet set. Load management: data centres prioritized above other loads for reduction under supply-related conditions; in standard operation, if firm load shed is needed in an emergency, data centres reduce before all other firm loads; procedures (pro rata, blocks, rotations) to be developed. 74.9 MW applications rose from 9 (Jun 2025) to 18 (Jun 2026) in the 25–75 MW band; AESO may lower the 75 MW threshold. Distribution-connected large loads bypass BYOG; AESO has limited tools for them. Final process was planned for late July–early August 2026 source rule quote to check Vancouver Zoning By-law s. 2 definitions and district schedules (2026): no stand-alone EV charging use — Parking Area/Garage "may include the retail sale of electricity for the purpose of charging motor vehicles" (Parking Uses conditional in I-1C, I-2, I-3, FC-2, M-1, IC-2, C-2); Urban Farm – Class B (may be in a greenhouse) conditional in all seven; no aquaculture term; Community Centre conditional in I-2, I-3, FC-2, M-1, C-2; Bulk Data Storage conditional in I-2 (not at ground floor except entrances), I-1C, FC-2, I-3 sub-area A source rule quote to check Edmonton Zoning Bylaw 20001 s. 8.10 use definitions: no EV charging use; Urban Agriculture ("hydroponic or aquaponic systems, and vertical farms") permitted in MU, IM, BE, CB, within or on a building (MU ≤600 m²); Community Service incl. shelters permitted in MU and BE (BE ≤500 m² except shelters); Minor Utility includes "district heating plants" (IM, BE); Major Utility includes "cooling plants" source
